Issued at 257 PM EDT Thu Oct 8 2026

120kt NW upper jet from Western Canada down into the Midwest and 
around into New England, circling around a 531dm 500mb upper low 
(and attendant 994mb surface low) in the vicinity of James Bay. 
Confluence zone aloft over the Mid-Atlantic...with Hurricane 
"Isaias" spinning over the Gulf, where the bulk of the deep moisture 
is focused attm; across the Southern Plains, some semblance of upper 
troughing. Upper jet is drawing some Pacific moisture across Western 
Canada into the Northern Plains; return flow over the central Plains 
helping to enhance convergence along western edge of a low-level 
baroclinic zone there, which stretches through the OH Valley into 
New England, around the base of the trough aloft. Some drier air 
sneaking into the Upper Great Lakes attm, though we do have some low-
level moisture around (plus the warm waters of the Great 
Lakes...still around 14-16C attm). Cool air to our north...0C at 
850mb over Lake Superior at 15z, with some -8C air well north over 
Hudson Bay attm. Temps here are just warm enough to generate some 
overlake instability, esp from approximately M-32 and northward; 
aided by some PV maxima tracking through the flow, a few showers 
over parts of the EUP and even into NE Lower this morning, which 
should hold on into at least part of the afternoon.

Subtle bit of energy crosses the area region Friday, but ridging 
builds in going into Friday night...as troughing digs into the 
western US...and Isaias tracks northward out of the Gulf. Looking at 
development of a stronger surface cyclone in the Northern Plains by 
Friday night into Saturday, resulting in strong warm advection 
through the Upper Midwest to start the weekend...which aside from 
summer-like temperatures could bring us a few showers Friday night 
into early Saturday. Currently, it appears troughing wants to cut 
off over the western US...with northern stream energy looking more 
progressive over Canada this weekend as Isaias tracks northward 
toward the OH Valley. Still some questions about how these features 
interact...but appears the baroclinic zone from the northern stream 
will stretch out to our north, and we may remain in a bit of a no-
man's-land between this and what is left of the tropical system for 
the first couple days of next week. Increasing uncertainty for the 
remainder of the period into the middle of next week...depending on 
how quickly ridging builds into the Midwest (likely depending on how 
strong the troughing out west ends up) and how the northern stream 
pattern evolves (this may again depend on how the troughing out west 
evolves...but there is some potential for the ridge to build quick a 
bit northward over the Midwest by midweek next week). The downside 
to this, as energy tries to eject from said trough...is that this 
pattern could certainly leave the Midwest open to a period of more 
active weather with a more active SW-NE storm track across the 
CONUS...though nothing is set in stone yet, by any means. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Cold Tonight...High pressure to our west expected to build in 
through the day into the night tonight, which should tamp down winds 
with time. Cool air mass in place suggests another frosty/freeze-y 
night for the area. Think the best shot of temps falling into the 
lower 30s or colder will be near and south of M-72, especially away 
from the lake...though not impossible it could get colder than 
forecast closer to Manistee/Beulah if the pressure gradient drops 
off fast enough tonight. Do wonder if upstream mid/high clouds on 
the nose of the jet max over southern Canada will be able to limit 
radiational cooling. Also wonder if we will end up with some fog 
tonight, given some recent rainfall, though we should mix down some 
drier air this afternoon. Not sure the widespread cold is a sure 
bet, given that we should still have some overlake instability and 
those aforementioned mid/high clouds, particularly near and north of 
M-72/M-32...and current temp forecast reflects this idea. If we 
clear out and calm down quicker across the Tip of the Mitt/EUP, 
temps would fall much more dramatically than currently forecast. 
Given Monday night's cold (widespread temperatures below 32F for 
northern Lower), will consider the growing season effectively ended 
(i.e., no more frost/freeze headlines for this season)...though 
suppose some areas near the Lake MI coast will remain more sensitive 
with a traditionally longer growing season. 

Warmth This Weekend...Warm front should move through during the 
first half of Saturday and result in much warmer conditions going 
into the afternoon than to start (plus we will likely have some 
clouds/rain around early Saturday morning along/ahead of the front). 
Much warmer air mass aloft will support temperatures rising into the 
mid and upper 70s; would not be surprised if some areas across NE 
Lower in particular (and perhaps TVC) touched or exceeded 80, given
